enterfront.body: This project is a simple chat application. It uses pseudo-database (API with a local variable) and short-pulling to access messages. Registration is performed also via API with the use of tokenization.
enterfront.history: It was an elective course Enterprise Programming on JS I have chosen at the the Fall semester 2024. I was in a team of 3 people, we were working during the period of 2 months. I was a team leader and made the biggest contribution to the project.
enterfront.ps: Project should work properly, try it! Register (or use one of predefined users e.g. 'alice' with password'1234') and type some id to start chatting (e.g. 'alice', 'evead', 'frank').

textyle.body: The idea is relatively simple: insert a text in any style, than convert it to the desired one. Then applying AI model that was connected with backend technics on Rust to the frontend on React.
textyle.history: This project was chosen as a topic of a Practicum Project course that was conducted in Summer 2024. We had 7 people at our team: team-leader, 2 frontend developers, 2 backend developers, 2 AI programmers.
textyle.ps: Unfortunately, the backend server as well as AI model wasn't hosted and ran locally during the presentation. Nevertheless, you can watch a video prepared for the final submission and demonstration.

fwd.body: This project doesn't pursue a complex idea, it's just demonstrating basic skills at the Frontend development. A user can observe a variety of different dishes that are published by restaurant admins. They can add it to their cart and calculate calories and price. Admins can post different dishes.
fwd.history: This is the final project for an elective course related the Frontend I took in Summer 2023. There was a small team of 2 people. However, for me this course and the project in particular were a starting point in the Frontend Development.
fwd.ps: The website works properly till the current but some links for meals are outdated and nonworking that's why some images are not displayed.

booking.body: The idea of the project: provide a convenient way to make bookings of university rooms for students and stuff. It was a telegram bot (with a Web App) that connected to an API related to booking of University rooms.
booking.history: It was a summer project (2023) at the core course for a team of 5. There were 2 frontend developers, including me.
booking.ps: There is no support for telegram bot anymore, however there is still a video about it. Enjoy watching it!

sna.short: System for periodical change of passwords
sna.body: This is an encoding systems that can periodically change password keys for security. It is used to create, store, and automatically update keys using a scheduler (a key updates once a day). It was implemented via Telegram Bot and Linux OS.
sna.history: I was working on this project during a course named Software Networks and Administration. I was the author of an idea for a project and the implementor of the hardest part of it (working with scheduler on Linux and returning updated key).
sna.ps: Initially, there wasn't even an idea to somehow host it, so there is only a video. It is relatively big (there were requirements of the course) but the most interesting part is at 6:25 (my college have explained before in the video that we have set update time to 22:27 instead of 00:00).

verilog.short: A 'computer game' on FPGA (in Verilog language)
verilog.body: It is a memory game: you to enter binary combinations (8 bits) using switches, where each combination corresponds to a part of a digit screen. The goal is to repeat a picture on the another screen without making a mistake. In case of a mistake, you need to start from the beginning.
verilog.history: I was participating in a voluntary project of Computer Architecture course. I was in a team of three, we were able to choose any theme we wanted but it had to be related to the programming on a FPGA board.
verilog.ps: Video contains a great music, we were glad that we could make this presentation more creative!

enigma.short: A Model of the Enigma machine
enigma.body: The Machine has 3 active rotors (you can choose out of 5), that rotates after pressing any key. When the first rotor makes full rotation, it rotates the second rotor on one position and so on. You need to enter letters one-by-one, then you will receive the output.txt with the encoded text. Repeat procedure to decipher.
enigma.history: I had seen a film about encoding and deciphering and wanted to dive deeper in this theme, so I wrote a C++ project that demonstrates how the Enigma machine works.
enigma.ps: I was practicing my German, so the video is made only in German. However, I have prepared English subtitles so you can turn on them.

game.body: Rules are simple: move a tank without crossing the borders of a battlefield, then make a shoot and hit a target! The goal: destroy all targets before you will out of ammo. Targets are placed each time time randomly.
game.history: I was at 10th year at school, I wanted to create something simple but interesting to interact with. So, I've written this game.
game.ps: You can watch a video or review a code I have uploaded to GitHub.

school.body: The telegram bot supports registration and choosing tracks (it is like a study program for a concrete subject). After that, a user can receive lectures and solve tests that correspond to a chosen track. Each test has deadlines (soft/medium/hard) that affect the score.
school.history: I decided to create an online school with my friend, my part was to write a useful and extendable telegram bot. However, a current state of a project is unfinished.
school.ps: The project is unfinished, the only option is to review a code.

compiler.body: The first stage of a compiler is lexer (lexical analyzer that splits program text to meaningful words like 'if', 'for', identifiers etc.), then comes parser (syntax analyzer that converts this words to a tree), then - validator or optimizer (semantics analyzer). Finally, generator converts it to machine commands for LLVM.
compiler.history: I've attended a Compiler Construction course. Our task was to write a compiler for a simple language that was developed by our Professor. The name of the language is I, it is an imperative language (functions and function calls). The project was implemented in the C++ language.
compiler.ps: You can watch a video or check the code on GitHub, moreover you can view presentation on Google slides.

naimix.body: It is an application for making prediction using Tarot cards (yeah, it was a task of the hackathon). The Frontend part takes a date of birth, calculate all data and sends it to the Backend, that in turn creates and sends a request to a Gigachat (AI model from Sber). After that, 'prediction' is displayed to a user.
naimix.history: At 15th of November 2024, we took part at this hackathon with a team of 5 members. I was developing a Frontend part: making some pages and connecting to a Backend part. Finally, we have taken 7th place out of 66 teams.
naimix.ps: Everything should work, you can try yourself our website! Moreover, you can check a short video if you wish.
